t: Count Triplets with Even XOR Set Bits II
o:
## Understanding the problem

Count triples (i, j, k) where popcount(a[i] XOR b[j] XOR c[k]) is even.

Example 1: 1^2^3 = 0, popcount 0 (even) → 1. Example 2: 1^3^1 = 3 (two bits, even) contributes 2×1×1 = 2; 1^2^5 = 110₂ (two bits, even) contributes 2×1×1 = 2; total 4.

The decisive fact: parity of popcount(x XOR y) = parity(x) + parity(y) (mod 2), because XOR cancels common bits and the parity of a sum of bits is linear. Hence the parity of the triple's XOR popcount is parity(a[i]) ⊕ parity(b[j]) ⊕ parity(c[k]). We only need, per array, how many elements have even vs odd popcount — values themselves are irrelevant!
k: popcount parity is additive under XOR: parity(x⊕y⊕z) = parity(x)⊕parity(y)⊕parity(z).
Count even-parity (e) and odd-parity (o) elements per array; the answer combines only these six counts.
Even total parity occurs for patterns (e,e,e), (e,o,o), (o,e,o), (o,o,e).

a.i: Bucket each array by popcount parity in O(n), then the number of triples with even combined parity is the sum of products over the four favorable parity patterns. This turns an apparently cubic problem into linear time.
s: For each array compute (even, odd) counts using popcount % 2.
Return the sum (fits in 64-bit: up to (10⁵)³ = 10¹⁵).
a.t: O(n) total — one popcount pass per array.

a.i: Triple-nested loops checking popcount(a[i]^b[j]^c[k]) % 2 == 0 directly. At n = 10⁵ per array this is 10¹⁵ operations — hopelessly slow, but useful as a correctness oracle when testing the combinatorial solution on small inputs.
s: Loop over all i, j, k.
Accumulate matches where the XOR has an even number of set bits.
a.t: O(|a|·|b|·|c|) — far too slow for the stated constraints.

w:
## Wrap-up

Always test parity claims against brute force on small random inputs — the linearity of popcount parity under XOR is the entire problem. Pitfalls: using 32-bit assumptions carelessly (values fit in 32 bits here, fine), and overflowing the product in 32-bit languages (use long/long long). Follow-up: count triples with popcount ≡ 1 mod 4, which needs per-array counts by popcount mod 4.
